title: Private KMS event mismatch causes SSO assertion truncation and audit gaps
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
A subset of Private clusters began dropping the tail of SSO/SAML assertions during token envelope rotation, producing truncated role claims and missing audit events. Customers report unexpected 403s for role-bound API calls and gaps in audit logs for the affected timeframe. Root cause appears to be a race between KMS envelope rotation metadata propagation and assertion verification logic that validates assertion integrity against a per-tenant key timestamp.

Impact:
- Several tenants (notably Acme Financial and OrbitRetail) experienced access failures for background inference jobs and Console UI actions between 2026-02-28T22:00Z and 2026-03-01T04:00Z.
- Audit events for assertion verification failures were intermittently not emitted, complicating post-incident analysis.
- Customer escalations received (severe SLA and compliance concerns).

Reproduction steps:
1) Configure a Private cluster with envelope-rotation interval set to 1h and enable KMS metadata caching.
2) Trigger a rotation + immediately issue SSO assertions with large attribute sets (~2-3KB).
3) Observe that assertion verification code sees a stale rotation marker and attempts an optimized path that assumes no envelope header; header bytes are misaligned and assertion payload is truncated, causing role claim parse errors.

Root cause hypothesis:
Metadata propagation for envelope rotation writes to the control-plane metadata collection and to instance-level cache. Under high concurrency the cache invalidation path was delayed; the verification code used a fast-path that omits re-fetch of envelope metadata if a local marker exists. When the marker was stale, verification attempted to rehydrate a KMS envelope with a mismatched event id, leading to partial read and truncated assertion payload. Audit emission was gated behind successful metadata reconciliation and got skipped when verification raised a specific AssertionParseException.

Proposed fix (hotpatch):
- Short-term: revert the fast-path in verification to always re-validate envelope metadata for assertions issued within the last 5 minutes of a rotation window. This reduces the window for race and allows audit emission to proceed consistently. Implement feature-guarded change so Dedicated/Hosted can opt-in later.
- Long-term: add idempotent metadata cohort writes and strengthen cache invalidation (follow-up: ENG-34901) and add end-to-end test coverage for rotation + assert flows.

Rollout plan:
1) Create a targeted hotfix image (runtime-private:2026.03.05-hotfix) building the verification change.
2) Canary deploy to two Private clusters (canary-1 and canary-2) with affected tenant profiles. Monitor for assertion failures and audit event counts for 2 hours.
3) If stable, roll forward across remaining Private clusters with 10% increments and automated rollback on error spike.
4) Notify customers and provide mitigation steps (see comments).

Telemetry/observability:
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/xyz/priv-kms-errors (query: rate(assertion.parse.errors[5m]))
- Sentry incident: https://sentry.redwood.com/organizations/redwood/issues/98765
- Incident writeup draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/PRIV+KMS+Event+Mismatch+Investigation
